classification.difficultyReason: Perform the supplied multi-step perpendicular-bisector constructions and compare the third bisector; familiar tools and a specified method, no hidden construction strategy or new theorem proof.

content.prompt: Points labelled O in this exercise are always centres of circles.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a large circle (and ignore the fact that you may be able to see the mark that the compasses made at the centre). Draw two non-parallel chords AB and PQ, then construct their perpendicular bisectors. The point where the bisectors intersect is the centre of the circle.

answer.short: Sample construction: the two perpendicular bisectors intersect at the centre O.
answer.worked: Draw a large circle without using its visible compass-centre mark. Choose two non-parallel chords AB and PQ. For each chord, use equal-radius compass arcs from its endpoints (radius greater than half the chord) to locate two equidistant points, then join them. Each resulting perpendicular bisector passes through the circle centre, so their intersection O is its centre.

spec.description: Sample only: nonparallel horizontal AB and vertical PQ are chords of radius2circle; their perpendicular bisectors x0/y0 meet true centreO, matching midpoint ticks/rightangles. No fixed student dimensions added.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Construct the perpendicular bisectors of two sides, and let them intersect at O. Construct the circle with circumcentre O passing through all three vertices of the triangle.

answer.short: Sample construction: O is the circumcentre; the circle of radius OA passes through A, B and C.
answer.worked: Construct the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC using equal compass arcs from their endpoints. Let their intersection be O. A point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is equidistant from A and B, and a point on the perpendicular bisector of BC is equidistant from B and C. Hence OA=OB=OC. Draw the circle with centre O and radius OA; it passes through all three triangle vertices.

spec.description: Sample only: A210/B330/C80 on radius2circle; perpendicular bisectors of AB/BC meet centreO, circle passes all3. BC perpendicular line slope .4663036 matches exact midpoint direction; no fixed student measurements added.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Construct the perpendicular bisector of the third side. It should also pass through O.

answer.short: The third perpendicular bisector also passes through O.
answer.worked: Construct the perpendicular bisector of CA in the same way. Since OA=OC, O lies on the perpendicular bisector of CA. Thus all three perpendicular bisectors meet at O; the third construction checks the same circumcentre.
